player.beatTargetNote: Focus is a Monroe state label, not “N hertz”. This Hz is an unverified |L−R| placeholder. Monroe Sound Science layers several EEG bands and changes them during a track.
player.analysisOff: Live FFT not running — play to start analysis.
player.analysisSilent: Audio plays, but the analyser sees no signal (often CORS). Spectrum stays empty.
player.detectHint: Live FFT: strongest tone per ear (80–1200 Hz). Estimated binaural beat ≈ |L − R|. Voice and music can dominate over Hemi-Sync carriers. A single peak is not the whole mix.
player.bandDistLabel: Live EEG-band mix in the audio (1–150 Hz)
player.bandDistHint: Share of stereo audio energy in Monroe UK EEG bands — FFT of the file, not your brain. δ 1–4 · θ 4–8 · α 8–13 · β 13–30 · γ 30–150 Hz. Mixes are layered and evolve; δ is poorly resolved (~5 Hz FFT bins).
player.ciaReportTitle: Why L / R / Beat? — CIA Gateway report (1983)
player.ciaReportBody: Hemi-Sync (CIA 1983): slightly different tones in each ear produce a binaural beat (|L − R|) via the frequency-following response. Monroe Sound Science: Focus labels are states of awareness, not a single Hz; tracks layer several bands (δ 1–4, θ 4–8, α 8–13, β 13–30, γ 30–150 Hz) and shift layers during the exercise. Headphones still required for binaural beats.
player.ciaReportSpectrum: The two spectra below show per-channel energy from 20 Hz to 4 kHz (log scale) — carriers, harmonics, and guided voice. The purple line marks a documented carrier when known.

glossary.title: Focus glossary
glossary.intro: Monroe labels for states of consciousness — a radio-dial, not a ladder you climb out of your body. Gateway home study lives mainly in 10, 12, 15 and 21. Focus 10 is not “10 Hz”.
glossary.phasing: The phasing model: awareness tunes in and out of states (daydream, deep relaxation, mystical experience) instead of “leaving” a physical body. C1 is ordinary waking life; higher numbers are other stations on the same dial.
glossary.bands: EEG bands (Monroe Institute UK): delta 1–4 Hz (deep sleep), theta 4–8 Hz (deep meditation), alpha 8–13 Hz (eyes-closed rest), beta 13–30 Hz (focused thinking), gamma 30–150 Hz (peak / breakthrough). Hemi-Sync / Sound Science layer several bands and change the mix during a session.
glossary.source: Focus map: Monroe Institute UK. EEG bands and layering: Monroe Sound Science. The 1983 CIA paper uses a shorter 10 / 12 / 15 / 21 map and treats those numbers more like beat rates.
